ops.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. **REGULATION (AU): the National Cabinet drought broke.** It met 26 August 2026 and published an outcome endorsing federal 'AI laws in Australia's Interests'. Three qualifications the headline coverage buries: the mandatory-standards content is **data-centre infrastructure regulation** (energy, water, land use) — no obligations on AI systems, agents or model providers were found; ABC reporting indicates leaders agreed to further work rather than settling standards, with **Queensland and NT refusing** the renewables clause; and legislation remains signalled for early 2027. Low direct relevance; the item to track is whether the 2027 bill carries a standards-making clause extensible beyond data centres. Note: this surfaced only under domain-constrained search — treat unconstrained AU searches as unreliable. **AGENT-TRUST STANDARDS: two new entrants, whitespace still holds.** Linux Foundation took governance of **TRACE** (25 Aug; AMD, Intel, Microsoft) — hardware-rooted runtime attestation proving an agent *ran under a policy in a verified environment*, not that it reasoned well. And a **W3C Agent Conformance and Benchmarking CG** was proposed (25 Aug), whose charter states plainly that nobody currently defines how conformance should be *measured*; its criteria (reproducible by an unrelated party, every check states the evidence it reads, fixtures that cannot be tuned to pass) are methodologically close to a deterministic assessment. FG-TIDA and NIST unchanged in-window. EU Article 50 settled and unchanged; no enforcement action found four weeks in. FUNDING: Carta Q2 2026 — $3.19B across 11,500+ pre-seed instruments, flat dollars on 22% fewer deals; average instrument $276k, a four-year high; AI holds half of pre-seed dollars. RISK: 'attestation' now has three well-funded referents; category confusion, not competition. OPPORTUNITY: the measurement gap is now stated by a standards body, not just inferred.

tech.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. **SECURITY (action this week): the Next.js release shipped 25 August — a day early, and with TWO criticals, not one.** GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4 is an unauthenticated RCE via Image Optimization on attacker-controlled AVIF (heap overflow in libheif via sharp), affecting **all 16.x through 16.3.2**; CVE-2026-75604 is a second unauthenticated RCE, **Windows filesystem only** — Linux and macOS unaffected, so it does not reach a Vercel deploy. **Fixed version is 16.3.3.** Vercel states hosted apps are protected because they disabled AVIF at the platform layer — but that does not patch the version in package.json, so local dev, CI and every scanner still see a vulnerable release. Before bumping, note 16.3.3 **disables AVIF optimization entirely** pending an upstream libheif fix. Affected-range and CVSS figures are secondary; confirm against the GHSA pages. **SUPPLY CHAIN: no new ChainDrop wave, no all-clear — but a persistence route worth knowing.** Reporting (StepSecurity, Microsoft, Elastic, via a secondary source) describes the worm writing a SessionStart hook into `.claude/settings.json` and a task into `.vscode/tasks.json` — configuration no lockfile audit reads, committed as 'chore: update config'. Relayed as a finding to verify, not acted on. ANTHROPIC: the Sonnet 5 price hold is **confirmed at primary source** — $2/$10 per MTok permanent, the 1 September rise cancelled. Caveat: Claude 4.7-and-later models use a tokenizer producing ~30% more tokens for the same text, so the saving is nearer break-even than headline. SUPABASE: nine incidents 17–30 Aug, two open, including **newly-refreshed JWTs being rejected** (PostgREST 14.17 rolled 27 Aug) — worth disambiguating from the known transient-401 class. Management API `logs.all` is removed 23 September. TYPESCRIPT: 7.1 stable now firm at **10 November**; typescript-eslint's TS 7 issue closed as not planned — treat TS 7 as Q1 2027. OpenSSL shipped nine CVEs on 25 Aug, none critical, patched by managed platforms. OPPORTUNITY: Batch API (50% off) and prompt caching remain the largest untaken cost levers for fixed-schema extraction.

growth.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. **COMPETITOR: daios.tech is materially more substantial than last week's 'active again' read implied.** Direct fetch found a revised preprint dated **18 August** ('A Disposition, Not a Rule: Virtue-Based Character Training'), reporting an honest negative result; an open **Sycophancy Benchmark** (260 scenarios, published rubric, runs against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint); Cosmos Institute funding; and backing from IBM, Notre Dame and Vercel. Their masthead reads 'σπουδαῖος — THE WISE SAGE'. Mechanism still differs (training-time LoRA adaptors vs inference-time attestation of how a decision was reasoned) — the collision is vocabulary and search real estate, not product. The vector to watch is the benchmark: it grades a *model's* tendency, but it is an evaluation artefact. Their blog is JS-rendered and did not fetch; the 24 Aug demo is corroborated, its outcome is not. **ECOSYSTEM: protocol governance consolidated.** Google's A2A joined the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (20 Aug), now 250+ members alongside MCP; an MCP v2.0 draft landed jointly from Anthropic and OpenAI (18 Aug), with the roadmap moving toward agent identity and delegated tasks. Okta shipped Agent SSO (26 Aug). Separately the AI AGENT Act (S.5051) directs NIST to standardise **proof-of-delegation and auditable records of agent actions** — provenance of permission, not quality of reasoning, but the same substrate. DEVREL: **llms.txt v2 shipped 10 August** — formal link relations, relaxed naming; a parallel W3C proposal (June) is not obviously reconciled with it, so watch before committing to the versioning-header form. Adoption is 5–15%. SEARCH: worse than the carried Pew figure — Chartbeat reports referrals down **60% for small publishers**, 22% for large; zero-click at 68%. STOIC: genuinely quiet. Stoic Week enrollment still not open (page untouched since 21 June); Stoicon 17 Oct unchanged; Stoicism Today has migrated to Substack, leaving the modernstoicism.com blog stale since January. Fortinet/Virtue AI: no closing news. RISK: Rubrik ships a product called SAGE in AI agent governance — SEO collision, not a competitor.

support.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. **CRISIS RESOURCES: all four verified current against official sources — 988 (US), Shout 85258 (UK), 9-8-8 (Canada), Lifeline 13 11 14 (AU). No change to any number, name, country label or availability. No action.** Funding is stable-to-improving: Canada renewed to March 2028 (CAD $120.2M/2yr); NSW committed AUD $43.3M over four years to Lifeline; SAMHSA opened a $231M administration opportunity. Scope note: the 988 LGBTQ+ youth 'Press 3' routing option was defunded July 2025 and refunded in the 2026 appropriations act — I could not confirm it is operating again; the main line is unaffected. **CORRECTION: Colorado HB 26-1195 is reported already IN FORCE — effective 12 August 2026**, not pending. It prohibits AI detecting emotions or mental states without licensed oversight; the crisis-guardrail carve-out still rests on the legislative record alone. **No AG guidance or FAQ exists** — three query formulations plus a domain-restricted coag.gov search. Also correcting: proposed rules were **filed 11 August** and the 23 September date is for interim updates to them; the **4 September deadline is four days away**, governing only revisions presented at the 26 October hearing (the portal itself runs to 26 October). Statutes effective 1 January 2027. Next imminent date elsewhere: **Connecticut's detect-and-respond duty, 1 October 2026**. Colorado's 2027 reporting will require **crisis-referral accuracy metrics** — regulators moving from 'have a protocol' to 'prove it works'. EU: Article 50(3) transparency for emotion-recognition systems took effect 2 August; high-risk duties deferred to December 2027. Australia: eSafety codes in force since March, penalties to AUD 49.5M, and eSafety found most companion services do **not** automatically refer on detected self-harm. QUIET: WCAG 3.0 unchanged (2.2 AA remains operative; ADA Title II deadlines extended to April 2027/2028); no philosophical-counselling development. RISK: state counts have moved (14 chatbot laws now reported) and sources disagree on the AI-therapy count. Statutory dates above come from law-firm briefings, not statute text — treat as reported, not read.
